mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, which raises discount rates and reduces present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the unemployment rate below 5% for three consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately reducing profit margins and producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in the industrial production index (INDPRO) above 0.5% for four consecutive months signals an acceleration in economic output, which typically coincides with higher corporate earnings and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in the federal funds rate and a decline in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) over two months indicates a successful disinflationary tightening, which supports risk asset valuations and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises AND CPIAUCSL falls over two months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated decline in both real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) by more than 1% month-over-month signals a broad-based collapse in demand, which depresses earnings and triggers negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and HOUST both fall > 1% MoM
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) above 200,000 for five consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, which supports consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: An always-on negative relationship exists between the real savings rate (RSAFS) and S&P 500 forward returns: higher real savings imply lower consumption, which reduces corporate revenue growth and yields negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.3%) in at least 55% of all trading days.
